segments.title: 第89章 約會
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years Chapter 89: Date

After a brief internal struggle, Li Luo still answered the phone.

Yan Zhusheng on the other end naturally had no idea about Li Luo's current situation and just said on her own, "I've asked about the matter."

"Didn't I tell you before? About the song arrangement, I entrusted it to an arrangement teacher. She's a friend of my mom's, and also a colleague."

"Later, I recorded a version of *Annual Rings* for her to see if there were any problems. As it turned out, my mom and a company executive happened to overhear it."

"Because you said to try not to mention to outsiders that you wrote the song, I didn't say who the writer was."

"As a result, my mom and the others thought I wrote it. That executive thought the song was quite good, and it just so happened that the company was preparing a theme song for a TV drama, so they recommended it."

"That's basically what happened. Now, the music has been initially decided. There will be five songs in total, used as the theme song, ending song, and interstitial background music."

"Your song has been selected, but it hasn't been confirmed whether it will be the theme song or something else."

"Of course, the copyright is in your hands, so whether you agree in the end will definitely be up to you."

Yan Zhusheng recounted the news she had gathered from Auntie Luo Fei, then asked, "Now that the preliminary results are out, the copyrights for those other songs are surely no problem, but I haven't asked you in advance."

"Before, because everyone thought it was my song, my mom didn't ask much. She knows I don't usually care about these things."

"But if it's you, I think it's better to ask beforehand. If you don't agree, I'll just have them switch to another song."

"What do you think?"

Li Luo listened quietly, temporarily pushing aside the fact that Yan Zhusheng already knew he wrote web novels.

He carefully considered it, then asked curiously, "If I agree, what are the specific details of the transaction? What about the price?"

"The production crew's total budget for the songs is about 200,000 RMB," Yan Zhusheng said honestly. "If it's chosen as the theme song, it should get a larger share, with the remaining four getting less."

After all, none of them were famous creators, and the drama *Tales of the Jasper Pool Immortals* wasn't a big production itself.

The money had all been spent on inviting the male and female leads. The male lead was a popular young heartthrob, and the female lead was one of the few well-known young starlets in recent years.

Before it even aired, the hype had already been maxed out by the fans.

But since they had spent too much on the actors, they naturally had to save wherever else they could.

For the music, they couldn't afford to hire the more famous people in the industry.

After all, with a single song passing through their hands, let alone 200,000 for five songs, 500,000 for one song was a common occurrence.

So, to be offered this price now seemed quite reasonable to Li Luo.

"Is it a full buyout of the song's copyright, or...?" Li Luo suddenly thought of a question and asked again.

"I'm not too sure about that." Yan Zhusheng frowned, then said, "But it probably isn't a full copyright buyout. I can help you ask about this again."

"I'll have to trouble you then," Li Luo said. "I have no problem on my end. If they need it, we can discuss the details."

"Oh, okay." Yan Zhusheng nodded. "I'll hang up then. I'll let you know when there's more news."

"Hey, wait," Li Luo said subconsciously, wanting to ask Yan Zhusheng about her reading his novel.

But the words reached his lips and were swallowed back down.

"What's wrong?" Yan Zhusheng asked, puzzled.

"Nothing..." Li Luo's mouth twitched. He thought about it and decided against it. "Hanging up. Talk later."

Placing his phone back on the desk, Li Luo sighed. Although his song *Annual Rings* had been noticed by the production crew by a twist of fate, allowing him to sell the copyright and earn some money, which put him in a good mood.

But...

He glanced again at the comment from "Sheng Sheng Bu Xi" in the comment section, and the pile of reader replies below it.

Isn't this the person who sang *Annual Rings*?

Tsk, tsk, you're telling me there's nothing scandalous going on? Why do I find that so hard to believe?

Miss, do you know Chong Ran offline? If you have time, help us mail him some razor blades.

Huh? Mo Faction? Even though I love your *Annual Rings*, Shen Dongdong is the best! Childhood friend for the win!

Looking down on my Yue Faction? Jiang Mingyue is number one in the world! An older-sister type is the ultimate answer! How can a little sister be better than an older sister?

You guys just don't get it. What if Mo Qinghan is Sheng Sheng Bu Xi herself? Look, she even gifted an Alliance Lord.

Li Luo: "..."

He had to admit, this bunch of readers were damn good at making wild guesses.

And the crucial thing was, sometimes they even managed to guess right.

After all, Li Luo hadn't known many girls in his past life. The three girls who had the biggest impact on his life were undoubtedly Ying Chanxi and the other two.

As a result, when he portrayed his female leads, he would more or less incorporate shadows of the three of them.

For example, the character Mo Qinghan, whom Yan Zhusheng had mentioned, was a young pop queen in the novel who was full of passion for music.

She was also the very pop queen at whose concert the protagonist found himself right after transmigrating at the beginning of Li Luo's book.

She was the first female lead to appear in the novel.

On the protagonist's path in his music career, she provided a great deal of help, and they became very important musical soulmates.

Hmm... Thinking about it this way, Li Luo understood why Yan Zhusheng would like this character.

And she had even gifted an Alliance Lord... Li Luo hadn't noticed before.

This meant that of his 12,000 RMB manuscript fee this month, 500 RMB had come from Yan Zhusheng.

But... the thought that everything he wrote from now on would be read by Yan Zhusheng made Li Luo feel uncomfortable all over.

Especially if he later wrote some scenes between Mo Qinghan and the protagonist that readers loved to see, the thought of Yan Zhusheng also seeing them gave Li Luo goosebumps.

It was too damn awkward!

However, since Yan Zhusheng hadn't exposed his author alias to his face, Li Luo tacitly pretended he hadn't found out.

He would just act like he didn't know.

Sticking his head in the sand was better than having Yan Zhusheng discuss the plot with him face-to-face in the future.

No wonder Yan Zhusheng had been listless for several days during the second week of school. It turned out she had been staying up late secretly reading his novel.

The corner of Li Luo's mouth twitched at this thought.

Just then, there was a knock on his bedroom door.

Ying Chanxi poked her head in from outside and said to Li Luo inside, "It's almost eleven! Come out for a walk with me!"

"Got it." Li Luo shut down his computer, got up, and tidied himself up. "Be right there. You get ready too."

A few minutes later.

Li Luo had changed into a loose-fitting sweatsuit, while Ying Chanxi wore a pink and blue dress with a wide-brimmed sun hat, looking youthful and beautiful.

"We're not going anywhere special, why did you dress up so nicely?"

"None of your business." Ying Chanxi shot him a look, slipped on her white sandals, and pattered out the door. "Hurry up, stop dawdling."

Li Luo followed behind, grabbed the keys, walked out, and after getting into the elevator, turned to get a closer look at Ying Chanxi's side profile.

Startled by his sudden proximity, Ying Chanxi's cheeks flushed slightly as she quickly asked, "What are you doing?"

"Nothing." Li Luo shook his head and asked curiously, "Did you put on makeup?"

"Um..." Ying Chanxi blinked, her gaze shifting away guiltily. "Just a little bit of foundation."

"Looks like you put on lipstick too."

"Just a little!"

"When did you buy makeup?" Li Luo was a bit surprised.

To be honest, since they went their separate ways before the high school entrance exams in his last life, Li Luo hadn't seen Ying Chanxi much. This was truly the first time he'd seen her with makeup on.

Even though it was just very basic, simple, light makeup, it was still a novel sight for him.

"I bought it secretly during summer vacation," Ying Chanxi said in a small voice. "Don't tell my dad, okay? I was just using it to practice."

"I can tell. It definitely looks like practice."

"What?" Hearing this, Ying Chanxi was instantly displeased. "Does it not look good?"

"It looks good, it looks good." Li Luo turned his head to scrutinize her again before concluding, "But that's purely because you have a good foundation to work with. It doesn't have much to do with your makeup skills. You might even look better without it."

Hearing him say this, Ying Chanxi lowered her head, the tips of her ears turning red, and she muttered under her breath, "You talk too much..."

The two of them went downstairs, walked out of the elevator, and headed out of the residential complex. Ying Chanxi then asked, "Where are we going?"

The area around Fuyi High School hadn't been developed much yet.

The subway wasn't connected, and the Longhu Tianjie mall next to Qianjiang University had yet to be built.

It was a transitional zone between the center of Yinjiang District and the suburbs.

But there was certainly no shortage of restaurants.

Li Luo took Ying Chanxi to a restaurant that looked relatively clean and bright, got a small private room, and ordered three or four small dishes for a simple meal.

The meal cost nearly a hundred RMB, which was definitely a huge expense for an average high school student.

But just as Li Luo was about to pay, Ying Chanxi beat him to it, pulling a crisp red Mao note from her small purse and handing it to the cashier.

"Your change is 7.50. Please take it."

Ying Chanxi took the change, stuffed it into her wallet, and looked at Li Luo. "Let's go."

"I should have treated you."

"I was the one who asked you out, so of course it's my treat," Ying Chanxi said with a grin. "If you want to treat me, please be a bit more proactive next time. Don't always make me ask you."

Ying Chanxi knew that Li Luo's family had taken out a loan to buy their house, so his allowance definitely wasn't much.

That's why there was no way she would let him pay such a large sum.

But after saying that, Ying Chanxi pointed to the milk tea shop across the street. "I want some milk tea."

Li Luo glanced at Ying Chanxi, roughly figuring out the girl's intentions, and smiled helplessly.

Being treated to a meal by a girl, and then having her be considerate of a guy's pride... it really was tough on her.

"What flavor do you want?"

"Just the regular pearl milk tea is fine."

"Not iced, right?"

"Eh? Um... yeah, I can't drink iced things these few days..."

(End of Chapter)
